vulnerabilities.description: Garmin password passed from request body to garmin_login_start(). While credentials are not persisted or logged, they transit through web request and exist in process memory during the handshake. MFA codes also held in memory.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Passwords in process memory during interactive Garmin login handshake

vulnerabilities.description: intervals.icu API key transmitted via Basic auth (Authorization header). While HTTPS ensures transit security, key is decoded from Authorization header in memory. No key rotation mechanism visible.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: API key in Basic auth header (intervals.icu upload)

vulnerabilities.description: Strava access token stored in sessionStorage (volatile) and transmitted in Bearer token Authorization header. SessionStorage is cleared on browser session end (good), but token can be accessed via devtools.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Strava OAuth token in sessionStorage (accessible via devtools)

vulnerabilities.description: Session tokens persisted to disk (~/.local/state/paceforge-runner/runs.jsonl) in plaintext JSON. File relies on OS file permissions (likely 0644 or 0600). Session tokens are 32-byte random strings with 180-day TTL.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Session tokens persisted to disk without encryption

vulnerabilities.description: GARMIN_TOKEN (base64-encoded tar.gz of token dir) decoded via tarfile.extractall() with filter='data'. While filter prevents path traversal, a compromised token blob could include symlinks or device files if tar format is fuzzy.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Tar extraction of GARMIN_TOKEN blob with minimal validation

vulnerabilities.description: Upload tokens (INTERVALS_KEY, STRAVA_KEY) cleared from old localStorage versions via try-catch, but removal errors silently ignored. Potential for orphaned tokens if removal fails.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Silent failure when purging legacy tokens from localStorage

vulnerabilities.description: Hand-rolled XML parser decodes HTML entities including numeric entities (&#x...;). No DTD/external entity prevention needed (lightweight parser), but error messages include parsed content without sanitization.
vulnerabilities.short_summary: XML entity decoding without error message sanitization

vulnerabilities.description: Failed login attempts trigger a global 1-second sleep (_LOGIN_BRAKE lock) per failed attempt. While this slows brute force, it's not exponential backoff. 10 parallel requests = 10 seconds total (not 1+2+4...). Timing attack risk on password comparison mitigated by hmac.compare_digest().
vulnerabilities.short_summary: Linear (not exponential) backoff on failed login attempts

scoreJustification: Single-athlete file-based architecture eliminates database/SQL injection risk. No API keys hardcoded. Token handling follows security-conscious patterns (env-based secrets, constant-time comparison, session TTL). Main risks are operational: credentials in transient memory during interactive flows (unavoidable), tokens on disk relying on OS file permissions, and upload token accessibility in browser storage (isolated per origin/path).
recommendations: Add NOPASSWD sudo path for Garmin token export CLI — avoids password prompt storage in env files. Use scrypt-verified file access instead.
Implement HMAC verification for GARMIN_TOKEN blob (sign base64 output with a server key) to detect tampering during tar extraction.
Add optional memory-locking for credentials in garmin_login_start() via mmap or ctypes to prevent core dump leakage (mlock-style, Python-only via resource module).
Upgrade failed login backoff to exponential (1s, 2s, 4s, ..., max 30s) to slow brute-force attempts from 10 parallel requests in 10 seconds to ~30+ seconds.
Document session token file permissions requirement (~/.local/state/paceforge-runner) — ensure created with 0600 mode (currently relies on umask).
Add Content-Security-Policy headers to prevent inline script injection in bike tab (escHtml is applied, but CSP as defense-in-depth).
Rotate Strava/intervals.icu tokens on each upload to minimize window of exposure if sessionStorage is dumped.
Add token-age warnings in /auth/whoami endpoint — surface token expiry to UI so stale Garmin OAuth tokens are surfaced before sync silently fails.

notes.architecture: Single-athlete per-instance; no shared backend. File-based data (JSON). VM runner at 127.0.0.1:8123 (public) + 127.0.0.1:8223 (internal/trusted). Caddy reverse-proxy fronts /paceforge/* with session requirement.
notes.secrets_handling: Environment-based (PACEFORGE_GARMIN_EMAIL, GARMIN_TOKEN, STRAVA_CLIENT_SECRET, etc.). .env files in .gitignore. Credentials never logged at INFO/DEBUG levels (verified via logging module usage).
notes.crypto: scrypt(n=2^14, r=8, p=1) for password hashing. hmac.compare_digest() for constant-time comparison. base64+gzip for token portability.
notes.session_management: Sessions dict in-memory + persisted to ~/.local/state/paceforge-runner/runs.jsonl. TTL 180 days. HTTPS-only transmission (Secure flag set). SameSite=Lax prevents cross-site cookie leakage.
notes.garmin_oauth: ~1-year refresh token (warns at 350 days). Stored in ~/.garminconnect/*.json. Materialized from GARMIN_TOKEN env var on startup (idempotent).
notes.sql_injection: Not applicable — no SQL database (file-based JSON).
notes.xss: escHtml() function in view.js for HTML escaping. Portal code reviewed for DOM injection — no obvious sinks. Needs CSP headers as additional layer.
notes.csrf: Session cookie scoped to PF_COOKIE_PATH (/paceforge or /pf/<name>). POST endpoints require session token. No explicit CSRF token needed due to same-site session isolation.
notes.dependencies: python-garminconnect, pydantic, requests (via garminconnect). No vendored secrets. Dependencies reviewed via pip audit (recommend: add to CI).
